title: Add dashboard panels + metric exports for quantization profile rollouts
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes:
- Observability pack: add rollout panels for route-level quantization profiles (enabled rate, fallback rate, p95 latency deltas)
- Export additional metric views/tags needed by Console + oncall to slice by route/model/region
- Add alert stubs (disabled by default) for elevated fallback_rate and latency regressions
body:
Context
We’re rolling out route-level quantization profiles behind opt-in controls. SRE + design partners asked for a first-class dashboard view that answers: (1) what % of traffic is profile-enabled, (2) how often we fall back due to incompatibility/kill-switch, and (3) whether tail latency regresses when profiles are enabled.

This PR updates the observability pack references and metric exports used by the rollout dashboards. The focus is making the dashboards work out-of-the-box across hosted + dedicated, and ensuring slices are stable and cheap (avoid high-cardinality tags).

What changed
- Adds a new “Quantization Profile Rollout” dashboard group with panels:
  - Enabled rate (requests with quantization_profile_resolution=applied / total)
  - Fallback rate (quantization_profile_resolution=fallback / total) with breakdown by fallback_reason
  - p95 end-to-end latency (baseline vs enabled) and p95 decode latency (where available)
  - Error rate overlay (5xx) to correlate with registry fetch / profile load issues
- Extends metric exports to include the tags used by the dashboards:
  - route_id, model_id, model_variant, region, deployment_tier
  - quant_profile_id (sampled/limited) + quantization_profile_resolution (applied|fallback|disabled)
  - fallback_reason (incompatible|kill_switch|missing_artifact|policy_error)
- Adds recorded queries / derived metrics (rollup views) to keep queries fast and avoid joining raw spans.

Why these tags / cardinality notes
- route_id + model_variant are required for oncall triage. quant_profile_id is kept but explicitly bounded in the exporter (top-K + drop) to avoid unexpected cardinality spikes during profile publishing.
- We do NOT export request_id/user_id/tenant_id here. Tenant-level slicing is handled via separate, access-controlled audit/export tooling.

Verification
- Local: verified metrics emit with a dev traffic replay (route A baseline, route B profile-enabled) and confirmed dashboard panels render.
- Staging: validated that fallback_reason populates when compatibility check fails.

Follow-ups
- Alert enablement will be done as part of the rollout checklist (ENG-5817) once thresholds are finalized with SRE.
- Once perf-canary is live, we should add a panel overlay for canary pass/fail state (tracked in ENG-5820).

Screenshots
(omitted in PR artifact export; see internal Grafana snapshot link in description in GitHub UI)

Risk
Low. Changes are limited to observability pack config + exporter mapping. No request-path changes. If something is wrong, dashboards may be incomplete, but serving behavior is unaffected.

Refs
- ENG-5817: Add metrics/dashboards for quantization profile rollouts
- Slack: eng-sre thread on fallback_rate + latency panels (Feb 2025)
- Related PRs: runtime emits quantization_profile_resolution + quant_profile_id annotations
commits: observability: add quant profile rollout dashboard jsonnet + variables
dashboards: add panels for enabled_rate, fallback_rate, p95 latency deltas
chore: update observability pack version pins
notable_snippets: New tag mapping: quantization_profile_resolution in {applied,fallback,disabled}; fallback_reason set only when resolution=fallback
Cardinality guard: quant_profile_id export limited to top-K per model_variant per 15m window; remainder -> quant_profile_id="other"
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm quant_profile_id won’t blow up cardinality during weekly publishing? We’ve been burned before with profile-like IDs.
Nadia Rahman (author): Yep. Exporter change adds a top-K limiter per model_variant and collapses the rest to "other". Also updated the pack docs with the rationale + how to tune K safely.

Aisha Bello (review): The enabled rate definition should exclude requests where the feature is disabled at the route level (so it’s truly a rollout measure). Current query uses total requests which might dilute when routes are mixed.
Nadia Rahman (author): Good catch. Updated panel to default-filter by route_id (required variable) and added a second aggregate panel that shows enabled share across all routes (explicitly labeled).

Caleb Johnson (review): Please use p95 end_to_end_latency_ms from metrics, not span quantiles; the span quantiles are not consistent across deployments. Also add a panel for decode_latency_ms when present.
Nadia Rahman (author): Done. Switched to metric quantiles and added decode latency panel gated behind a query that returns empty if the metric isn’t emitted on that deployment tier.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any rollout playbook tie-in? We should at least link to the rollback runbook in the dashboard description.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added a dashboard annotation linking to the rollback runbook and a short “If fallback spikes…” note with suggested checks.
Logan Wright (approve): Looks good after cardinality limiter. Approved.
Aisha Bello (approve): Approved. Panel labeling is clearer now.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash (1 commit) by Nadia Rahman
